title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: in-product diagnostics for case access, security filters and holds
summary: The documented control paths, commands, licensing background and current rollout windows are supported. The statement that every rollout date was postponed goes beyond the supplied notice, and the search-filter command should acknowledge a difference between Microsoft's guide and its cmdlet reference.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery is introducing in-product diagnostics.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery is introducing three read-only diagnostic checks for case access, security filters, and hold-policy distribution.

claims.claim: There are three checks, covering case access, security filters and hold-policy distribution.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery is introducing three read-only diagnostic checks for case access, security filters, and hold-policy distribution.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The new diagnostic checks are read-only.
claims.quote: Admins can use three read-only diagnostics to understand common issues with case access, search scoping, and hold-policy distribution.

claims.claim: The checks provide troubleshooting guidance.
claims.quote: The diagnostics provide guidance without changing your organization's existing configuration.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The checks do not change the organisation's existing configuration.
claims.quote: The diagnostics provide guidance without changing your organization's existing configuration.

claims.quote: Self-service diagnostics help identify common issues with case permissions, security filters, and policy status.

claims.quote: The experience highlights potential misconfigurations and provides simple guidance to help customers understand and resolve them.

claims.claim: The notice moved each rollout date later than its earlier schedule.
claims.quote: Searched: the supplied MC1515937 rollout schedule and its 'previously' comparisons. It gives earlier preview dates, all earlier GA starts and an earlier Worldwide GA completion, but no earlier GCC, GCC High or DoD completion dates.
claims.fix: Replace 'The notice moved each date later than its earlier schedule.' with 'The notice postponed the preview start and completion, all GA start dates, and the Worldwide GA completion date.' The supplied MC1515937 explicitly gives those comparisons.

claims.claim: MC1515937 names eDiscovery admins as the affected group.
claims.quote: Who is affected: - eDiscovery admins.

claims.claim: Microsoft says no admin action is required at this time.
claims.quote: No admin action is required at this time.

claims.claim: MC1515937 sets no act-by date.
claims.quote: Act by: none. No admin action is required at this time.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the new three-check experience as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery in-product diagnostics hold' and 'eDiscovery diagnostics case access security filters'; read edisc-permissions, edisc-settings-access-permissions, edisc-hold-manage and purview-compliance-diagnostics. Results describe existing controls and older diagnostics, not the new experience.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented where the new checks appear in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview eDiscovery in-product diagnostics case access security filters hold distribution diagnostic permissions roles prerequisites enabled default turn off'; read purview-compliance-diagnostics and edisc-permissions. Their Help-pane paths concern existing diagnostics.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented exactly what each new check inspects.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery diagnostics case access security filters' and 'eDiscovery in-product diagnostics hold'; read edisc-permissions, edisc-hold-manage and purview-compliance-diagnostics. MC1515937 names the three areas but not the detailed inspections.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the specific role needed to run the new checks.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview eDiscovery in-product diagnostics case access security filters hold distribution diagnostic permissions roles prerequisites enabled default turn off'; read edisc-permissions and purview-compliance-diagnostics. Existing role rules do not identify the role for these three new checks.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an admin switch to turn the new diagnostics on or off.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview eDiscovery in-product diagnostics case access security filters hold distribution diagnostic permissions roles prerequisites enabled default turn off'; read edisc-get-started, edisc-permissions and purview-compliance-diagnostics. No switch for the new checks was found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The default state of the new checks is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview eDiscovery in-product diagnostics case access security filters hold distribution diagnostic permissions roles prerequisites enabled default turn off'; read MC1515937, the roadmap, edisc-get-started and purview-compliance-diagnostics. None states their default enablement.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not said what data the new checks read or display.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery diagnostics case access security filters' and 'eDiscovery in-product diagnostics hold'; read purview-compliance-diagnostics, edisc-settings-access-permissions and edisc-hold-manage. No new-check results or displayed data are specified.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated prerequisites specific to the new checks.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview eDiscovery in-product diagnostics case access security filters hold distribution diagnostic permissions roles prerequisites enabled default turn off'; read edisc-get-started and edisc-permissions. General eDiscovery prerequisites exist; no additional check-specific prerequisites were found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not said whether the new checks appear for case members who are not eDiscovery admins.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview eDiscovery in-product diagnostics case access security filters hold distribution diagnostic permissions roles prerequisites enabled default turn off'; read edisc-permissions and MC1515937. The notice names admins, without specifying availability to other case members.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed how the new diagnostics read the existing case membership, role, filter and hold controls.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery diagnostics case access security filters' and 'eDiscovery in-product diagnostics hold'; read edisc-settings-access-permissions, edisc-permissions, edisc-search-permission-filtering and edisc-hold-manage. None maps the new checks to those settings.

claims.claim: The notice mentions no automatic remediation.
claims.quote: The diagnostics provide guidance without changing your organization's existing configuration.

claims.claim: The case-access article says a user must be added to the eDiscovery Manager role group before accessing a case.
claims.quote: before a user can access an eDiscovery case (and perform tasks in the case), you must add the user to the eDiscovery Manager role group in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The permissions article also documents eDiscovery permissions through Compliance Administrator, Organization Management and Reviewer role groups.
claims.quote: you can also assign users eDiscovery-related permissions by adding them to the Compliance Administrator, Organization Management, and Reviewer role groups.

claims.claim: Users who are not eDiscovery Administrators see only cases they belong to.
claims.quote: For users who aren't eDiscovery Administrators, the cases shown are limited to those where the user is a member.

claims.claim: An eDiscovery Administrator can view and access all cases.
claims.quote: An eDiscovery Administrator can view and access all eDiscovery cases, they can audit and oversee all cases and associated compliance searches.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Adding or removing a role in a role group automatically removes that group from every case it belongs to.
claims.quote: If you add or remove a role from a role group that you added as a member of a case, the role group is automatically removed as a member of the case (or any case the role group is a member of).

claims.claim: Search permissions filters restrict which mailboxes, sites or content an eDiscovery manager can search.
claims.quote: Use search permissions filtering to let an eDiscovery manager search only a subset of mailboxes and sites in your organization. You can also use permissions filtering to let that same eDiscovery manager search only for mailbox or site content that meets a specific search criteria.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The existing eDiscovery RBAC diagnostic checks whether Search, Export or Preview roles are assigned to a named user.
claims.quote: Run the following diagnostic test to check if the Export, Preview, or Search roles are assigned to the designated admin account.

claims.claim: The existing RBAC diagnostic is reached in the Purview portal through Help > Ask a question > search for Diag:edisRBACdiag.
claims.quote: Select the Help icon in the upper-right corner of the portal. In the Help and support pane, select Ask a question. In the search box, enter a brief description of the issue that you want to resolve.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Existing Help-pane diagnostics are unavailable in GCC High, DoD and Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet.
claims.quote: Diagnostics in the Help pane aren't available in the following environments: GCC High, DoD, and Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet.

claims.claim: Assigning eDiscovery permissions requires Organization Management membership or the Role Management role.
claims.quote: You need to be a member of the Organization Management role group or be assigned the Role Management role to assign eDiscovery permissions in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Running compliance security filter cmdlets requires Organization Management role group membership.
claims.quote: To run the compliance security filter cmdlets, you need to be a member of the Organization Management role group and have the eDiscovery administrator role assigned in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Running compliance security filter cmdlets also requires the eDiscovery administrator role.
claims.quote: To run the compliance security filter cmdlets, you need to be a member of the Organization Management role group and have the eDiscovery administrator role assigned in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Compliance security filter cmdlets run through Security & Compliance PowerShell with Exchange Online PowerShell also connected.
claims.quote: You need to connect to both Exchange Online and Security & Compliance PowerShell to use the compliance security filter cmdlets.

claims.claim: eDiscovery Manager role assignment is at Settings > Role groups > eDiscovery Manager > Edit > Manage eDiscovery Manager > Choose users or Choose groups in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Role groups. On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select eDiscovery Manager. Select Edit. On Manage eDiscovery Manager, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group> adds a security group to the eDiscovery Managers subgroup.
claims.quote: You can add a mail-enabled security group as a member of the eDiscovery Managers subgroup in the eDiscovery Manager role group by using the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell. Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group>

claims.claim: Case members are added at eDiscovery > Cases > case > Case settings > Access and permissions > Users or Role groups > Add in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Select a case, then select Case settings. On Case settings, select Access and permissions. Under Users, select Add to add users to the case. You can also choose to add a role group to the case by selecting Add under Role groups.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{ediscoveryCaseId}/caseMembers adds a user or role group to a case.
claims.quote: Add an ediscoveryCaseMember to an ediscoveryCase. The ediscoveryCaseMember can be one of two types: a user or a role group. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/b0073e4e-4184-41c6-9eb7-8c8cc3e2288b/caseMembers

claims.claim: The Graph case-member request body sets recipientType.
claims.quote: recipientType | microsoft.graph.security.recipientType | Specifies the recipient type of the eDiscovery case member. The possible values are: user, roleGroup, unknownFutureValue. Required.

claims.claim: The Graph case-member request identifies the member using id, displayName for a role group, or smtpAddress for a user.
claims.quote: id | String | The ID of the eDiscovery case member. If not specified, then either displayName (for role group) or smtpAddress (for user) must be provided.

claims.claim: A portal path for configuring search permissions filters is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery search permissions filtering portal UI configure security filters New-ComplianceSecurityFilter Get-ComplianceSecurityFilter'; read edisc-search-permission-filtering and the New-ComplianceSecurityFilter reference. Results document PowerShell configuration, not a portal route.

claims.claim: New-ComplianceSecurityFilter -FilterName <name of filter> -Users <user or role group> -Filters <filter> creates a search permissions filter.
claims.quote: Use the New-ComplianceSecurityFilter cmdlet to create a search permissions filter. Here's the basic syntax for this cmdlet: New-ComplianceSecurityFilter -FilterName <name of filter> -Users <user or role group> -Filters <filter>
claims.fix: Keep the guide-supported call, but append to the row note: 'The cmdlet reference additionally marks -Action as mandatory; it selects Search, Preview, Export, Purge or All.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-compliancesecurityfilter?view=exchange-ps, whose syntax and -Action parameter table differ from the cited guide.

claims.claim: Hold retry is at eDiscovery > Cases > case > Hold policies > hold policy > Policy actions > Retry policy in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Select the eDiscovery solution card, then select Cases in the left navigation. Select a case, then select the Hold policies tab. On the Hold policy page for the selected policy, select Policy actions > Retry policy.

claims.claim: Set-CaseHoldPolicy -Identity <policyname> -RetryDistribution retries hold-policy distribution.
claims.quote: Run the Set-CaseHoldPolicy -Identity "policyname" -RetryDistribution to resolve the issue.

claims.claim: Get-CaseHoldPolicy -Identity <policyname> -DistributionDetail reads hold-policy distribution status.
claims.quote: Check whether a hold policy is pending before you make any further updates to it. $status = Get-CaseHoldPolicy -Identity <policyname> -DistributionDetail

claims.claim: Get-ComplianceSecurityFilter lists existing search permissions filters.
claims.quote: Use Get-ComplianceSecurityFilter to return a list of search permissions filters. Use the FilterName parameter to return information for a specific search filter.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft documents Microsoft 365 Enterprise E3 or E5 licensing for both admins and users working with eDiscovery cases.
claims.quote: Both admins and users working with eDiscovery cases require a Microsoft 365 Enterprise E3 or E5 license.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included in the licence eDiscovery already requires, with no diagnostics-specific entitlement yet published.
claims.quote: Both admins and users working with eDiscovery cases require a Microsoft 365 Enterprise E3 or E5 license.

claims.where: summary; front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: A licence, add-on or consumption charge specific to the new diagnostics has not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview eDiscovery in-product diagnostics license pricing charge billing'; read edisc-get-started, edisc-permissions and edisc-billing, plus the roadmap and MC1515937. claims.claim: Analysing a user's data with premium features requires Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5, or a Microsoft Purview Suite or Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-on for eligible E1/E3 users.

claims.claim: The cited permissions and case-access articles do not themselves mention the new diagnostics.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery diagnostics case access security filters'; read edisc-settings-access-permissions and the relevant roles, assignment and RBAC sections of edisc-permissions. The former has no diagnostic; the latter documents the existing RBAC Help diagnostic, not the new checks.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The known incremental cost of the new checks is indirect admin time, with diagnostics-specific licensing not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview eDiscovery in-product diagnostics license pricing charge billing'; read edisc-billing, edisc-get-started, the roadmap and MC1515937. No direct diagnostic charge was found. The rationale limits the low rating to known preparation effort, not a claim of free use.

claims.claim: MC1515937 does not mention end users or case reviewers as affected groups.
claims.quote: Who is affected: - eDiscovery admins.
